report: The lung tissue exhibits cells with eosinophilic cytoplasm, hyperchromatic nuclei, and high nucleus-to-cytoplasm ratios, suggesting cellular stress or pathology. Loose cell arrangements and potential alveolar structures indicate lung tissue architecture, with areas of thickened alveolar walls and extracellular matrix or fibrin deposits. Presence of red blood cells and signs of hemorrhage or inflammation may indicate organizing pneumonia.

evidence.title: Various antibody clones of Napsin A, TTF-1, and p40 in non-small cell lung carcinoma
evidence.text: This tissue-microarray study evaluated CK5, p63, and p40 as squamous markers and Napsin A and TTF-1 as lung adenocarcinoma markers. Reported performance varied by marker and antibody clone, and combining Napsin A with TTF-1 improved sensitivity.

evidence.title: Educational case: basal cell carcinoma and its histologic differential
evidence.text: Basal cell carcinoma shows dermal islands of basophilic tumor cells with peripheral nuclear palisading, stromal retraction, and loose mucinous stroma. Cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma shows invasive islands of pleomorphic keratinocytes arising from the epidermis with prominent nucleoli and increased mitoses. Melanoma can show irregular nests and single pleomorphic pigmented melanocytes within the epidermis and dermis.

evidence.title: Immunostaining for TTF-1, Napsin A, p40, and cytokeratin 5 aids differential diagnosis of NSCLC
evidence.text: The study compared marker combinations for separating lung adenocarcinoma from squamous cell carcinoma. TTF-1 and Napsin A supported adenocarcinoma, while p40 and CK5 supported squamous differentiation; the combined panel was more informative than a single stain.

evidence.title: Value of napsin A and thyroid transcription factor-1 in the identification of primary lung adenocarcinoma
evidence.text: In a cohort containing primary lung cancers and metastases, Napsin A and TTF-1 were frequently expressed in primary lung adenocarcinoma. The study also observed TTF-1 expression outside lung adenocarcinoma, supporting interpretation as a panel rather than as an isolated marker.

evidence.title: Histologic features of herpes simplex virus esophagitis
evidence.text: HSV esophagitis can show ulceration, necrotic debris, multinucleated giant squamous cells, ground-glass or eosinophilic intranuclear inclusions, nuclear molding, and chromatin margination. Viral immunohistochemistry or another confirmatory method may be needed because viral esophagitis patterns can overlap.

The study compared marker combinations for separating lung adenocarcinoma from squamous cell carcinoma. TTF-1 and Napsin A supported adenocarcinoma, while p40 and CK5 supported squamous differentiation; the combined panel was more informative than a single stain.

review.assessment: The vision models predominantly suggest lung adenocarcinoma, but the provided pathology report describes non-specific inflammatory and architectural changes rather than definitive malignancy.
rationale: The report describes 'eosinophilic cytoplasm' and 'thickened alveolar walls' suggesting organizing pneumonia, which does not definitively align with the glandular or lepidic patterns of lung adenocarcinoma [PMID:26447895, PMID:26137020].
Vision models CONCH, MUSK, and QUILTNET baseline favor lung adenocarcinoma, but the report lacks mention of mucin or glandular formation required for this label [PMID:22966403].
PLIP's classification of kidney renal clear cell carcinoma is unsupported by the report's description of lung tissue architecture.
discrepancies: The pathology report suggests a benign or inflammatory process (organizing pneumonia), whereas the vision models predict malignant carcinomas.
Lack of immunohistochemical data (e.g., TTF-1, p40) in the report to differentiate between adenocarcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma as discussed in [PMID:26447895].
recommended_review: Human pathologist review to differentiate between organizing pneumonia and malignancy.
Immunohistochemical staining for TTF-1, Napsin A, and p40 to resolve the NSCLC differential.
limitations: The de-identified report is descriptive and lacks a definitive diagnostic conclusion.
